entries.title: Psalms 66:1
segments:
. The writer invites all men to unite in praise, cites some striking occasions for it, promises special acts of thanksgiving, and celebrates God's great mercy. 
 
    1. Make ... noise--or, "Shout."

entries.title: Psalms 66:2
segments: 2. his name--as in

. 
 
    make his praise glorious--literally, "place honor, His praise," or, "as to His praise"; that is, let His praise be such as will glorify Him, or, be honorable to Him.

segments:

entries.title: Psalms 66:5
segments: 5, 6. The terrible works illustrated in Israel's history (

entries.title: Psalms 66:7
segments: 7. behold the nations--watch their conduct.

entries.title: Psalms 66:8
segments: 8, 9. Here is, perhaps, cited a case of recent deliverance.

segments: 9. holdeth ... in life--literally, "putteth our soul in life"; that is, out of danger (

entries.title: Psalms 66:10
segments: 10-12. Out of severe trials, God had brought them to safety (compare

segments: 11. affliction--literally, "pressure," or, as in

, "oppression," which, laid on the 
 
    loins--the seat of strength (

entries.title: Psalms 66:12
segments:
12. men to ride over our heads--made us to pass. 
 
    through fire, &c.--figures describing prostration and critical dangers (compare

). 
 
    wealthy--literally, "overflowing," or, "irrigated," and hence fertile.

entries.title: Psalms 66:13
segments: 13-15. These full and varied offerings constitute the payment of vows (

entries.title: Psalms 66:15
segments:
15. I will offer--literally, "make to ascend," alluding to the smoke of burnt offering, which explains the use of "incense." 
 
    incense--elsewhere always denoting the fumes of aromatics.

entries.title: Psalms 66:16
segments: 16-20. With these he unites his public thanks, inviting those who fear God (
, His true worshippers) to hear. He vindicates his sincerity, inasmuch as God would not hear hypocrites, but had heard him.

entries.title: Psalms 66:17
segments: 17. he was extolled with my tongue--literally, "exaltation (was) under my tongue," as a place of deposit, whence it proceeded; that is, honoring God was habitual.

entries.title: Psalms 66:18
segments: 18. If I regard iniquity in my heart--literally, "see iniquity with pleasure."
